subject: reference group in multiple group CFA

messages.author: 356316b848e93292
messages.subject: reference group in multiple group CFA
parts:
Hi all, 

I am conducting measurement invariance testing using multiple group CFA, and would like to compare latent means across three groups. The latent mean for the reference group was fixed at zero and freely estimated in the other two groups. The group variable has three levels: 0,1,2.

However, I am not sure how lavaan determined which group to be the reference group? Is it the smallest from the three levels in the group variable (so in my example, 0 would be the reference group)? If so, what can I do if I want to change the reference group to another group?

Much thanks in advance,
Frank

messages.author: ff3a366aa7a9b488
messages.subject: Re: reference group in multiple group CFA
parts:
Hi Quanfa He or Frank,

The "reference group" is the one in which the mean is fixed at zero. Ultimately, however, this is completely irrelevant. You can analyze the mean differences between the groups separately from the "reference group" if you define parameters. How to do that has probably been explained here many times - although I didn't look for it explicitly.

Best

Christian

messages.subject: Re: reference group in multiple group CFA
parts:
On 7/15/22 23:26, 'Quanfa He' via lavaan wrote:
> However, I am not sure how lavaan determined which group to be the
> reference group?

It is the first group as it appears in your dataset. If you wish to
choose a diffferent group as the 'reference' group, you can change the
order of the groups by using the group.label= argument. See ?lavOptions.

For example:

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, group = "school",
group.label = c("Grant-White", "Pasteur"))

Yves.

messages.author: ff3a366aa7a9b488
messages.subject: RE: reference group in multiple group CFA
parts:
Hi Frank,

Let's start with a simple 3 group model and simulate some data:

library(lavaan)

 

pop.model <- "f =~ 1.0 * x1 + 0.9 * x2 + 0.9 * x3"

 

n = 10000

set.seed(1)

data <- rbind(

  simulateData(paste(pop.model, "f ~ 1.0 * 1", sep = "\n"), sample.nobs = n),

  simulateData(paste(pop.model, "f ~ 2.0 * 1", sep = "\n"), sample.nobs = n),

  simulateData(paste(pop.model, "f ~ 2.4 * 1", sep = "\n"), sample.nobs = n)

)

data$g <- rep(1 : 3, each = n)


The mean of the lv in the first group is 1.0, the mean of the lv in the second group is 2.0, and the mean of the lv in the third group is 2.4. We specify the model and set an arbitrary mean value for the lv in any group. This group is now the "reference group". We specify the mean differences using parameters:

model <- "

f =~ x1 + x2 + x3

f ~ c(m1, m2, m3) 

m1 == 10

diff.g2.g1 := m2 - m1

diff.g3.g1 := m3 - m1

diff.g3.g2 := m3 - m2

"

 

In our case, the mean value of the lv in the first group is 10. The first group is thus the "reference group". We fit the model and obtain the correct mean differences:

fit <- cfa(model, data, group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"), meanstructure = TRUE, group = "g")

pe  <- parameterestimates(fit)

pe[pe$op == ":=",]


Since we can also set the mean of the "reference group" to zero (which is common), two out of three mean differences are provided "free of charge":

model <- "

f =~ x1 + x2 + x3

f ~ c(m1, m2, m3) * 1

m1 == 0

diff.g2.g1 := m2 - m1

diff.g3.g1 := m3 - m1

diff.g3.g2 := m3 - m2

"

 

fit <- cfa(model, data, group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"), meanstructure = TRUE, group = "g")

pe  <- parameterestimates(fit)

pe[pe$op == "~1" & pe$lhs == "f",]

pe[pe$op == ":=",]


One could come up with the idea to completely abandon the definition of a "reference group" by applying effect coding:

model <- "

f =~ x1 + x2 + x3

f ~ c(m1, m2, m3) * 1

diff.g2.g1 := m2 - m1

diff.g3.g1 := m3 - m1

diff.g3.g2 := m3 - m2

"

fit <- cfa(model, data, effect.coding = TRUE, group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"), meanstructure = TRUE, group = "g")

pe  <- parameterestimates(fit)

pe[pe$op == ":=",]


Note: The results are obviously biased (which was to be expected)!

HTH

Christian

Since we can also set the mean of the "reference group" to zero (which is common), two out of three mean differences are provided "free of charge":

 

model <- "

f =~ x1 + x2 + x3

f ~ c(m1, m2, m3) * 1

m1 == 0

diff.g2.g1 := m2 - m1

diff.g3.g1 := m3 - m1

diff.g3.g2 := m3 - m2

"

 

fit <- cfa(model, data, group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"), meanstructure = TRUE, group = "g")

pe  <- parameterestimates(fit)

pe[pe$op == "~1" & pe$lhs == "f",]

pe[pe$op == ":=",]

 

One could come up with the idea to completely abandon the definition of a "reference group" by applying effect coding:

 

model <- "

f =~ x1 + x2 + x3

f ~ c(m1, m2, m3) * 1

diff.g2.g1 := m2 - m1

diff.g3.g1 := m3 - m1

diff.g3.g2 := m3 - m2

"

fit <- cfa(model, data, effect.coding = TRUE, group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"), meanstructure = TRUE, group = "g")

pe  <- parameterestimates(fit)

pe[pe$op == ":=",]

 

Note: The results are obviously biased (which was to be expected)!

HTH

 

Christian

  simulateData(paste(pop.model, "f ~ 2.4 * 1", sep = "\n"), sample.nobs = n)

)

data$g <- rep(1 : 3, each = n)

f =~ x1 + x2 + x3

f ~ c(m1, m2, m3) 

m1 == 10

diff.g2.g1 := m2 - m1

diff.g3.g1 := m3 - m1

diff.g3.g2 := m3 - m2

"

fit <- cfa(model, data, group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"), meanstructure = TRUE, group = "g")
